notes: Parts are unchanged from step 1; all are catalogue types.

Each pushbutton straddles the centre gap. Side 1 (1.l top-half leg, 1.r bottom-half leg) is the column that carries the Arduino signal pin and the pull-down resistor. Side 2 (2.l, 2.r) is the column that carries +5V. Pressing the button joins +5V to the signal pin.
Button columns: btn1 at 6/8, btn2 at 11/13, btn3 at 16/18, btn4 at 21/23, btn5 at 26/28. The columns were read off the circuit image.
Pin mapping from the image and schematic: btn1 on pin 6, btn2 on pin 5, btn3 on pin 4, btn4 on pin 3, btn5 on pin 2. Each 10k resistor goes from the signal column to the GND rail, as a pull-down.

The image's top half of the breadboard is named bank 't' and its bottom half bank 'b', following the catalogue naming. The +5V rail is 'tp' and the GND rail is 'bn'. Exact rail hole numbers (tp.3, tp.8, tp.14, tp.18, tp.23, tp.28, bn.6 to bn.26, bn.30) are approximate positions taken from the image. Every hole on a rail is the same strip.
Arduino 5V goes to the + rail with the red wire. GND goes to the bottom - rail with the black wire, using the GND header pin next to 5V (GND.1).
